features.name: Document Import
features.description: Users can import .txt and .md files via ImportPanel with file picker
features.evidence: ImportPanel previously relied on Electron's File.path, which was removed in Electron 32+ (project uses ^33.2.0) and made import silently broken. Replaced with a main-process file picker: added SELECT_IMPORT_FILE IPC channel backed by dialog.showOpenDialog (filtered to .txt/.md), exposed via preload as documents.selectImportFile(), and wired ImportPanel's 'Choose File' button to it. Import errors now surface in the panel instead of being swallowed. Verified DocumentService.importDocument end-to-end (import/list/get/delete) by running compiled dist/services code directly against a temp file. tsc -p tsconfig.node.json (main/preload/shared/services) and vite build both succeed with no new errors; could not launch the actual Electron window in this sandbox because the electron binary is not installed (network-restricted environment).

features.name: Document Detail with Content
features.description: DocumentDetail shows full document content, metadata, and delete button
features.evidence: DocumentDetail had a TODO where content loading was never implemented (state was declared but never set). Added GET_DOCUMENT_CONTENT IPC channel backed by DocumentService.getDocumentContent (already existed), exposed via preload as documents.getContent(id), and wired DocumentDetail to fetch and display it in a useEffect keyed on document.id. Metadata display and delete button were already present and unaffected. Verified DocumentService.getDocumentContent returns correct text via direct service-level test against a temp file. tsc -p tsconfig.node.json and vite build succeed; could not launch the actual Electron window in this sandbox (electron binary not installed).

features.name: Basic Persistence
features.description: Imported documents persist across app restarts via filesystem storage
features.evidence: PersistenceService and DocumentService already write documents-meta.json and content/<id>.txt on every import/delete. The only missing piece was that App.tsx never called refreshDocuments() on mount — documents stored on disk would not appear in the list on relaunch. Fixed by adding a useEffect(() => { refreshDocuments(); }, []) in App.tsx. Verified end-to-end at the service layer: imported a doc via DocumentService, then constructed fresh PersistenceService + DocumentService instances against the same data directory (simulating a restart), called listDocuments() and getDocumentContent() — both returned the correct data. tsc -p tsconfig.node.json succeeds with no new errors. Electron binary not installed in this sandbox so the window cannot be launched directly.
